newsitem.title: CHINA: China to launch probe of state firm officials.
newsitem.headline: China to launch probe of state firm officials.

text.p: China is to launch a probe of officials in state-owned firms to try to curb graft and stem losses, the Economic Daily said on Monday.

Offices of the ruling Communist Party and the State Council, or cabinet, would start inspections this year aimed at ferreting out corruption and ushering in reform-minded officials, the newspaper said.
The probe would evaluate the work of officials, partly based on information provided by workers, and would include checks of companies' accounts and tax information, the newspaper said.
"Some (officials) misuse their power, use their authority for personal gain or even violate laws and discipline by wantonly squandering and misappropriating state assets," it said.
Many officials did not have the political will to carry out badly needed reforms of state firms while others took advantage of their positions to demand bribes, it said.
"A large number of facts prove that having a good leading group is crucial to doing a good job with state-owned enterprises," it said.
It did not say what would happen to officials deemed to be unfit to lead a company or who broke the law.
Losses by state-owned firms included in the national budget soared to 52.99 billion yuan ($6.38 billion) in 1996, up 38.8 percent from the year before, official figures show.
About 75 percent of China's more than 100,000 state firms lost money last year, with total losses in the sector rocketing 45 percent to 69 billion yuan between January and October.
Beijing has been reluctant to push ahead with reform of state enterprises for fear that bankcruptcies could cause mass unemployment and spark social unrest.
